data.answer:
The best patent-scope classifier in the 2024 study was the **multilayer perceptron (MLP)**, which achieved an **F1 score of 0.780** for classifying patents as broader or not broader, using first and all claims.[1] F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall—not the percentage of predictions classified correctly.[2]

The model actually deployed for the report’s analysis used three categories—narrower, similar and broader—and achieved a slightly lower **F1 score of 0.772**.[3]

claims.text: The best patent-scope classifier in the 2024 study was the MLP, with an F1 score of 0.780 for broader versus not broader using first and all claims.

citations.quote: F1 - The harmonic mean of Precision and Recall.
Accuracy - The fraction of predictions the modelling correctly predicted

claims.text: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, rather than the percentage of predictions classified correctly.

citations.quote: Ultimately, Narrower v. Similar v. Broader (with "scope3" as the target variable) was deployed to produce the data used in the descriptive and regression analyses in the main text.
| First & All | Narrower, Similar, Broader | MLP Classifier | 0.772 |

claims.text: The model deployed for the report’s analysis classified patents as narrower, similar or broader and achieved an F1 score of 0.772.
